purpose: machine-facing knowledge base of concrete explanatory and decision work-units for how banks, credit, and payment systems work, supporting grounded retrieval, evaluation, and synthesis within a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: subdomain of Money, Banking & Macro-Finance scoped to bank mechanics, credit, payment systems, and digital money
nodes are concrete explanatory/decision work-units, not institutions or products
no observed dataset supplied; all metrics are heuristic priors
key reference framing draws on Mishkin, The Economics of Money, Banking, and Financial Markets
exclusions: macroeconomic monetary-policy forecasting beyond bank-facing plumbing
securities markets, insurance, and asset management mechanics
jurisdiction-specific legal drafting and individual product pricing engines
investment trading strategy and corporate-finance valuation

competency_questions.question: How do a bank's assets, liabilities, and equity define bank money and its solvency vs liquidity?
How do banks create deposit money by lending, and what limits that creation?
What makes a bank's funding and capital position fragile or resilient (liquidity vs solvency)?
When and why does a solvent bank still fail, and how does a run spread?
How do reserves, the policy-rate corridor, and the lender of last resort work?
What are the steps from loan application to underwriting decision, pricing, and workout?
How is credit risk quantified into expected loss, and how do collateral and haircuts reduce it?
How do credit scores drive lending decisions, and what fairness risks do they carry?
How do banks earn the interest spread, and how does rate risk move net interest margin?
What are the layers and parties of a payment system, and what is settlement finality?
Which payment rail or card network fits a use-case given speed, finality, reversibility, and cost?
What payment fraud and operational risks exist per rail, and what controls mitigate them?
How do blockchains, stablecoins, and CBDCs work, and what run and peg risks do they carry?
What compliance perimeter bounds banking/credit/payments, and how are mechanics synthesized into a grounded answer?

glossary.definition: deposit claims on banks that circulate as money, distinct from central-bank money
central-bank balances held by banks, an asset of the bank
equity buffer that absorbs losses before depositors, a ratio not an asset pool
ability to meet outflows on time, distinct from being solvent
PD x LGD x EAD, the mean credit loss over a horizon
a model-derived rank of default risk used in decisioning
net interest income relative to interest-earning assets
exchange and reconciliation of payment instructions before settlement
the legally irrevocable transfer of value between parties
the fee transferred between acquirer and issuer on a card transaction
a crypto token aiming to hold a stable value via backing or algorithm
a digital central-bank liability available to the public or wholesale users

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: model heuristic priors for banking, credit, and payment work-units

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Frame what bank money is and how a bank's assets/liabilities/equity define its solvency and liquidity position.
contradictors: analyst who treats deposits as bank cash on hand

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when money aggregates, accounting rules, or the asset mix are redefined

pros.claim: an explicit balance-sheet frame prevents confusing deposits (a liability) with cash
pros.example: deposits sit on the liability side; loans are assets

cons.claim: an implicit frame makes every later mechanic (reserves, capital, runs) ambiguous
cons.example: treating a deposit as the bank's own money mis-states liquidity

acceptance_tests: money aggregates (M0/M1/M2) and bank-money distinction stated

nodes.definition: Explain how banks create deposit money by lending, holding only fractional reserves, and the limits on that creation.

included: reserve vs capital vs demand limits

contradictors: textbook 'money multiplier' literalist ignoring demand-led creation
outputs: binding-constraint map (capital vs reserves vs demand)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the binding constraint shifts between reserves, capital, and loan demand

pros.claim: clarifies that loans create deposits, not the reverse
pros.example: a new loan simultaneously books an asset and a matching deposit

cons.claim: naive multiplier framing overstates mechanical control of the money stock
cons.example: claiming reserves x multiplier fixes lending ignores capital and demand limits

acceptance_tests: loan-creates-deposit mechanism shown on the balance sheet
binding constraint identified for a stated regime

nodes.definition: Characterize deposit and wholesale funding, maturity transformation, and the liquidity risk it creates.
contradictors: analyst who assumes deposits are permanently stable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when funding mix shifts to flightier wholesale or uninsured deposits

pros.claim: separates cheap sticky core deposits from flighty wholesale funding
pros.example: insured retail deposits are stickier than overnight repo

cons.claim: maturity transformation is structurally fragile to coordinated withdrawal
cons.example: borrowing short to lend long breaks if depositors leave fast

failure_modes: liquidity coverage assumed adequate without test
acceptance_tests: funding mix decomposed by stickiness and insurance status
maturity gap and liquidity buffer stated

nodes.definition: Explain regulatory capital, risk-weighting, and leverage limits that set how much loss a bank can absorb.
contradictors: analyst conflating capital (a ratio) with reserves (an asset)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when capital rules, risk weights, or the leverage ratio change

pros.claim: capital is the buffer that keeps insolvency from following loan losses
pros.example: CET1 absorbs losses before depositors are touched

cons.claim: risk-weighting can be gamed, understating true leverage
cons.example: zero-weighting sovereign debt hides concentration risk

failure_modes: risk weights treated as ground truth
acceptance_tests: capital ratio defined against risk-weighted and total assets

nodes.definition: Model self-fulfilling deposit runs, liquidity-solvency interaction, and contagion across the banking system.
contradictors: analyst who treats a run as purely a solvency event

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when funding fragility, capital weakness, or confidence shocks co-occur

pros.claim: explains why solvent banks can still fail on liquidity and coordination
pros.example: a maturity-mismatched solvent bank fails if depositors run first

cons.claim: run dynamics are nonlinear and hard to predict from any single ratio
cons.example: the same balance sheet survives or fails depending on confidence

acceptance_tests: run modeled as a coordination failure with a self-fulfilling equilibrium

nodes.definition: Explain reserves, the policy rate corridor, open-market operations, and lender-of-last-resort backstops.
contradictors: analyst who ignores the corridor and quotes one 'the rate'

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the operating framework (corridor vs floor) or facility terms change

pros.claim: connects bank lending and runs to the central-bank backstop and rate setting
pros.example: the discount window converts a liquidity crisis into a solvency test

cons.claim: operating frameworks differ across regimes, so one description does not generalize
cons.example: a floor system behaves differently from a scarce-reserve corridor

nodes.definition: Describe the credit lifecycle: origination, underwriting decision, pricing, monitoring, and workout.
contradictors: lender who prices without assessing default risk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when credit policy, risk appetite, or pricing inputs change

pros.claim: organizes credit work into an auditable approve/price/monitor lifecycle
pros.example: a documented decision links default-probability to the rate offered

cons.claim: process can be sound yet still mis-price if risk inputs are biased
cons.example: good workflow over a bad PD model still under-prices risk

nodes.definition: Quantify credit risk via probability of default, loss given default, and exposure at default into expected loss.
contradictors: analyst who equates a credit score with a default probability

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when PD/LGD/EAD inputs or the macro scenario change materially

pros.claim: decomposes loss into PD x LGD x EAD so each driver can be managed
pros.example: EL = PD x LGD x EAD makes collateral and exposure levers explicit

cons.claim: point estimates hide tail risk and correlation across borrowers
cons.example: low average PD still implies large losses if defaults correlate

acceptance_tests: expected loss expressed as PD x LGD x EAD

nodes.definition: Explain how collateral, haircuts, and seniority reduce loss given default and shape secured-credit terms.
contradictors: lender who books collateral at market value with no haircut

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when collateral valuations, haircuts, or legal perfection change

pros.claim: collateral lowers LGD and aligns incentives, reducing expected loss
pros.example: a perfected lien on liquid collateral cuts loss given default

cons.claim: collateral value is procyclical and can evaporate exactly when needed
cons.example: fire-sale haircuts widen in the stress when collateral is called

nodes.definition: Explain credit scores/scorecards, their inputs, and how they drive automated lending decisions and fairness concerns.
contradictors: modeler who uses proxies for protected attributes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when scorecard features, regulations, or population drift change

pros.claim: turns heterogeneous borrowers into a comparable, auditable risk rank
pros.example: a scorecard maps attributes to a default-rank with reason codes

cons.claim: scores can encode bias and degrade under population drift
cons.example: a proxy feature can produce disparate impact across groups

nodes.definition: Explain how banks earn the spread between asset yields and funding costs and how rate risk affects net interest margin.
contradictors: analyst who treats the spread as fixed across rate cycles

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when the rate environment or the asset/funding repricing mix changes

pros.claim: links profitability to the gap between lending yields and funding cost
pros.example: NIM rises when asset repricing outpaces deposit-cost repricing

cons.claim: spread compresses with deposit competition and rate inversion
cons.example: an inverted curve squeezes a borrow-short lend-long book

nodes.definition: Frame the layered architecture of payments: instruments, clearing, and settlement, and the parties at each layer.
contradictors: analyst who collapses clearing and settlement into one step

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a new instrument, scheme, or settlement layer enters scope

pros.claim: separates instruction (clearing) from final value transfer (settlement)
pros.example: an authorized card payment clears instantly but settles later

cons.claim: layer boundaries blur in newer rails, inviting category errors
cons.example: instant rails compress clearing and settlement, hiding risk timing

nodes.definition: Explain netting, settlement finality, and the difference between deferred-net and real-time-gross settlement.
contradictors: analyst who assumes a payment is final at authorization

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when netting arrangements or finality/settlement timing change

pros.claim: makes settlement finality and netting risk explicit and timed
pros.example: DNS nets exposures intraday; RTGS settles each payment with finality

cons.claim: netting hides bilateral exposures until a participant fails
cons.example: a defaulting member can unwind a multilateral net batch

acceptance_tests: settlement finality point identified for each rail
settlement-risk window and netting unwind risk stated

nodes.definition: Compare bank payment rails (ACH, wire/RTGS, instant) on speed, finality, reversibility, and cost.
contradictors: analyst who treats ACH and wire as interchangeable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a rail's finality, speed, or reversibility characteristics change

pros.claim: matches each payment use-case to the right rail by finality and cost
pros.example: wires are fast and final; ACH is cheap, batched, and reversible

cons.claim: reversibility and speed trade off, creating fraud/settlement tension
cons.example: irrevocable instant rails remove the chargeback safety net

nodes.definition: Explain the four-party card model, interchange, authorization-clearing-settlement flow, and chargebacks.
contradictors: analyst who ignores interchange and the four-party split

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when scheme rules, interchange, or the authorization flow change

pros.claim: explains who pays whom across issuer, acquirer, network, and merchant
pros.example: interchange flows from acquirer to issuer on each card sale

cons.claim: two-sided pricing makes incidence (who really bears fees) non-obvious
cons.example: merchant fees may be passed to consumers via prices

nodes.definition: Identify payment fraud types, operational and settlement risk, and the controls that mitigate them.
contradictors: analyst who treats fraud loss as a fixed cost of doing business

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when fraud patterns, rail reversibility, or control coverage change

pros.claim: ties fraud exposure to each rail's reversibility and authentication model
pros.example: irrevocable rails shift loss to the payer and demand stronger auth

cons.claim: controls add friction and false positives that cost legitimate volume
cons.example: aggressive fraud rules decline good customers

acceptance_tests: fraud taxonomy mapped to rails and controls

nodes.definition: Explain blockchains, consensus, and crypto-asset settlement as an alternative ledger and value-transfer model.
contradictors: promoter who claims trustless finality with no settlement risk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when consensus mechanisms, settlement assumptions, or asset types change

pros.claim: frames crypto as a distinct ledger/settlement model, not just an asset
pros.example: on-chain settlement replaces a trusted intermediary with consensus

cons.claim: probabilistic finality and volatility undercut money-of-account use
cons.example: reorgs mean 'final' settlement is statistical, not legal

failure_modes: probabilistic finality treated as legal finality

nodes.definition: Explain stablecoin designs, backing/redemption, and the run and peg risks of tokenized private money.
contradictors: issuer who claims a peg without verifiable reserves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when backing composition, redemption terms, or peg confidence change

pros.claim: maps stablecoin stability to reserve quality and redemption credibility
pros.example: fully-reserved redeemable tokens resist runs better than algorithmic ones

cons.claim: tokenized private money inherits classic bank-run fragility
cons.example: an under-collateralized or opaque-reserve stablecoin can break its peg

acceptance_tests: backing and redemption mechanism verified against run scenarios

nodes.definition: Explain central-bank digital currency design choices and their tradeoffs for privacy, disintermediation, and stability.
contradictors: advocate who ignores bank-disintermediation risk

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when design choices (account vs token, caps, remuneration) or objectives change

pros.claim: structures CBDC choices around explicit policy tradeoffs
pros.example: holding caps limit disintermediation but weaken the use-case

cons.claim: a retail CBDC can drain bank deposits and amplify runs
cons.example: flight to risk-free CBDC accelerates a stressed bank's run

acceptance_tests: claim validated against the node definition and source before finalization

nodes.definition: Frame the regulatory and AML/KYC perimeter governing banks, credit, and payments and its compliance obligations.
contradictors: operator who treats compliance as optional overhead

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when regulations, sanctions regimes, or reporting thresholds change

pros.claim: defines the legal perimeter every banking/payment activity must respect
pros.example: KYC/AML obligations gate onboarding and transaction monitoring

cons.claim: compliance is jurisdiction-specific and changes faster than systems
cons.example: a sanctions update can outpace screening-system updates

acceptance_tests: AML/KYC and sanctions obligations enumerated by jurisdiction

nodes.definition: Integrate bank, credit, and payment mechanics into a defensible, source-grounded explanation or decision for a query.
contradictors: explainer who asserts conclusions without grounding or caveats

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when any upstream mechanic, evidence, or the query context changes

pros.claim: forces integration and explicit caveats before any claim is issued
pros.example: a payment-finality claim is tied to the specific rail and jurisdiction

cons.claim: synthesis can launder upstream errors into a confident wrong answer
cons.example: a clean narrative over a bad credit-risk input misleads decisively

acceptance_tests: every claim traced to a node and source with stated caveats
material assumptions and uncertainty explicitly recorded

edges.why_related: credit creation is read off the balance-sheet frame
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling creation before the balance sheet yields category errors
edges.example: loan booked as asset + deposit liability
edges.resolution_rule: fix the balance-sheet frame before credit creation

edges.why_related: funding/liquidity is a view of the liability side
edges.benefit_of_coupling: liquidity analysis grounded in the balance sheet
edges.risk_of_conflict: liquidity analysis without the frame mislabels deposits
edges.example: deposit ladder built on liability map
edges.resolution_rule: define the balance sheet before liquidity

edges.why_related: capital is the equity buffer in the balance-sheet frame
edges.benefit_of_coupling: solvency tied to equity, not reserves
edges.risk_of_conflict: capital confused with reserves without the frame
edges.example: CET1 located in equity

edges.why_related: payments move balances defined on the balance sheet
edges.benefit_of_coupling: payment value transfer grounded in money types
edges.risk_of_conflict: payment modeling without money types confuses settlement
edges.example: settlement debits a reserve balance

edges.why_related: crypto is contrasted against bank-money mechanics
edges.benefit_of_coupling: crypto framed as an alternative ledger
edges.risk_of_conflict: crypto explained without bank-money baseline overclaims novelty
edges.example: on-chain vs deposit settlement
edges.resolution_rule: establish bank money before crypto contrast

edges.why_related: the central-bank backstop and rate corridor shape credit creation limits
edges.benefit_of_coupling: creation limits tied to the operating regime
edges.risk_of_conflict: plumbing without creation mechanics misreads constraints
edges.example: corridor sets the marginal funding cost

edges.why_related: lending is the micro act through which credit is created
edges.risk_of_conflict: underwriting detached from creation misframes capital cost
edges.example: each approved loan creates a deposit

edges.why_related: run risk is driven by funding fragility and maturity mismatch
edges.benefit_of_coupling: run model grounded in funding structure
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling runs without funding structure misses the trigger
edges.example: wholesale flight starts the run

edges.why_related: capital adequacy conditions whether a run becomes insolvency
edges.benefit_of_coupling: run severity tied to loss absorbency
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring capital makes run outcomes indeterminate
edges.example: thin capital turns a liquidity run into failure

edges.why_related: holding more capital/liquidity buffers lowers leverage and return on funding
edges.risk_of_conflict: over-optimizing returns erodes buffers that prevent runs
edges.example: leverage boosts ROE but raises fragility
edges.resolution_rule: prudential floor dominates; safety over yield when buffers near minima

edges.why_related: expected loss quantifies the risk the underwriting decision takes
edges.risk_of_conflict: underwriting without EL under-prices risk
edges.example: rate set below PD x LGD x EAD

edges.why_related: collateral primarily acts by reducing LGD in the EL model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: secured terms grounded in loss decomposition
edges.risk_of_conflict: collateral valued without LGD linkage overstates protection
edges.example: perfected lien cuts LGD

edges.why_related: scoring operationalizes default risk into a decision rule
edges.risk_of_conflict: scores used without risk grounding become opaque
edges.example: score ranks PD for cutoff

edges.why_related: expected credit loss is a cost that the spread must cover
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring EL inflates apparent margin
edges.example: NIM net of credit cost is the real spread

edges.why_related: funding cost is one leg of the net interest margin
edges.risk_of_conflict: margin computed without funding cost is meaningless
edges.example: deposit beta drives funding cost

edges.why_related: clearing and settlement are layers within the payments architecture
edges.benefit_of_coupling: finality analysis grounded in the layer map
edges.risk_of_conflict: settlement modeled without the architecture conflates steps
edges.example: auth clears; net settles later

edges.why_related: each bank rail instantiates a clearing/settlement design
edges.benefit_of_coupling: rail comparison grounded in settlement mechanics
edges.risk_of_conflict: comparing rails without settlement theory misranks them
edges.example: RTGS=gross final; ACH=deferred net

edges.why_related: card flows are a clearing/settlement instance with extra parties
edges.risk_of_conflict: card flow without settlement view hides risk timing
edges.example: auth then batch clearing then settlement

edges.why_related: a rail's reversibility/finality determines its fraud exposure
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fraud model grounded in rail properties
edges.risk_of_conflict: fraud analyzed without rail finality misjudges loss incidence
edges.example: irrevocable wire fraud is unrecoverable

edges.why_related: card dispute/chargeback design shapes fraud loss allocation
edges.benefit_of_coupling: fraud model grounded in scheme rules
edges.risk_of_conflict: card fraud without chargeback rules misallocates loss
edges.example: chargeback shifts loss to merchant/issuer

edges.why_related: bank rails and card networks are parallel payment instruments
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating them as identical loses the four-party distinction
edges.example: both move value but differ in parties
edges.resolution_rule: keep distinct; compare on finality and party model

edges.why_related: lender-of-last-resort availability changes run outcomes
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the backstop overstates run inevitability
edges.example: discount window halts a liquidity run

edges.why_related: stablecoins are built on the blockchain settlement model
edges.benefit_of_coupling: stablecoin analysis grounded in ledger mechanics
edges.risk_of_conflict: stablecoins explained without the ledger miss settlement risk
edges.example: token transfers settle on-chain

edges.why_related: stablecoins inherit deposit-run fragility from maturity/backing mismatch
edges.benefit_of_coupling: peg-run risk grounded in run theory
edges.risk_of_conflict: treating stablecoins as run-proof ignores classic fragility
edges.example: reserve doubt triggers a redemption run
edges.resolution_rule: apply run theory to stablecoin peg

edges.why_related: CBDC sits inside central-bank money and plumbing
edges.benefit_of_coupling: CBDC tradeoffs grounded in monetary operations
edges.risk_of_conflict: CBDC designed without plumbing misjudges monetary impact
edges.example: CBDC as a new central-bank liability

edges.why_related: a retail CBDC competes with bank deposits, risking disintermediation
edges.risk_of_conflict: an unconstrained CBDC drains funding and amplifies runs
edges.example: flight to CBDC in stress
edges.resolution_rule: design caps/remuneration so CBDC does not gut deposit funding

edges.why_related: private stablecoins and public CBDC compete to provide digital settlement money
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring the rivalry misframes the policy choice
edges.example: CBDC may crowd out or regulate stablecoins
edges.resolution_rule: policy chooses the mix; financial-stability mandate dominates

edges.why_related: lending operates within the compliance and fair-lending perimeter
edges.risk_of_conflict: lending outside the perimeter creates legal exposure
edges.example: KYC gates onboarding before credit

edges.why_related: payments operate within AML/sanctions monitoring obligations
edges.risk_of_conflict: payment flows without AML controls breach the perimeter
edges.example: transaction monitoring on each rail

edges.why_related: fair-lending law constrains which features a scorecard may use
edges.risk_of_conflict: unconstrained scoring risks disparate-impact violations
edges.example: banned proxy features removed

edges.why_related: rising credit losses erode capital and can precipitate solvency-driven runs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: run risk linked to asset quality
edges.risk_of_conflict: ignoring asset quality understates run probability
edges.example: a loss spike thins capital and sparks doubt
edges.resolution_rule: feed credit losses into run assessment

edges.why_related: fraud controls and AML monitoring share detection infrastructure
edges.risk_of_conflict: siloing fraud and AML duplicates and misses typologies
edges.example: shared monitoring flags fraud and laundering

edges.why_related: stability findings feed the integrated explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesizing without stability view yields unsafe claims
edges.example: explain fragility before reassurance

edges.why_related: credit-risk results feed the integrated explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesis without credit results mis-states loss
edges.example: ground a lending claim in EL

edges.why_related: settlement-finality facts feed the integrated explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesis without finality facts mis-times risk
edges.example: tie a finality claim to the rail

edges.why_related: digital-money risk findings feed the integrated explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesis without peg risk overstates stability
edges.example: caveat a stablecoin claim with reserve risk

edges.why_related: compliance constraints bound the integrated decision
edges.risk_of_conflict: synthesis ignoring compliance proposes illegal actions
edges.example: gate a recommendation on KYC/AML

edges.why_related: profitability context informs the integrated explanation
edges.risk_of_conflict: omitting margin context weakens business framing
edges.example: frame a pricing answer with NIM

conflict_axes.trigger: raising buffers lowers leverage and return; chasing return thins buffers
resolution_order: accept lower return as the cost of stability
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: prudential safety dominates when buffers approach minima; otherwise optimize return within the floor
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: buffer falls below regulatory minimum or stress threshold
conflict_axes.example: increasing leverage to lift ROE just before a funding shock

conflict_axes.trigger: a stressed bank may be illiquid, insolvent, or both, demanding different remedies
resolution_order: diagnose whether the shortfall is funding or capital
apply liquidity support only if solvent
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: solvency diagnosis dominates the choice of remedy; liquidity support must not mask insolvency
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: liquidity support requested by a possibly-insolvent bank
conflict_axes.example: lending to a bank that is actually insolvent delays loss recognition

conflict_axes.trigger: volume targets pressure underwriting to loosen standards
resolution_order: price every loan above its expected loss
forgo volume that breaches the limit
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: expected-loss pricing dominates volume targets; growth that is not risk-priced is rejected
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: portfolio PD drifts up while origination accelerates
conflict_axes.example: chasing market share by approving thin-file borrowers below price

conflict_axes.trigger: predictive features can encode disparate impact on protected groups
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: fair-lending compliance dominates marginal predictive gain from a suspect feature
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a feature improves accuracy but fails a disparate-impact test
conflict_axes.example: a zip-code proxy raising AUC while harming a protected class

conflict_axes.trigger: instant irrevocable settlement removes the chargeback/recall safety net
resolution_order: match rail finality to fraud exposure of the use-case
add stronger authentication for irrevocable rails
retain a reversible rail where dispute risk is high
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: fraud-loss control dominates raw speed when the payer cannot bear irrevocable loss
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: high-fraud use-case routed to an irrevocable instant rail
conflict_axes.example: authorized-push-payment fraud on an instant rail with no recall

conflict_axes.trigger: an attractive retail CBDC can disintermediate banks and amplify runs
resolution_order: assess disintermediation under normal and stress states
apply holding caps or tiered remuneration
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: financial-stability mandate dominates; CBDC convenience is capped to protect deposit funding
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: projected deposit outflow to CBDC exceeds a stability threshold
conflict_axes.example: uncapped CBDC accelerating a stressed bank's deposit flight

conflict_axes.trigger: private and public digital money compete to provide settlement and store of value
resolution_order: weigh innovation and choice against systemic and monetary-control concerns
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: systemic-stability and monetary-singleness concerns dominate the public-private mix decision
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a private stablecoin reaches systemic scale
conflict_axes.example: a dominant stablecoin functioning as shadow money of account

conflict_axes.trigger: new rails and products outpace AML, sanctions, and consumer-protection coverage
resolution_order: map the new activity to the compliance perimeter
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: compliance perimeter dominates launch speed; uncovered activity is blocked until controls exist
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a product would go live outside AML/sanctions coverage
conflict_axes.example: launching a cross-border rail with no sanctions screening

conflict_axes.trigger: simplifying a mechanic for a lay audience can drop load-bearing caveats
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness and material caveats dominate simplicity; accessibility never removes a load-bearing caveat
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: a simplification would change the decision implied
conflict_axes.example: calling a payment 'instant and final' without naming the rail's actual finality

edge_cases.trigger: a deposit is treated as the bank's own spendable cash
edge_cases.example: claiming a bank 'lends out deposits' as cash
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether deposits are placed on the liability side and loans as assets
resolution: show loan-creates-deposit on the balance sheet

edge_cases.trigger: the money multiplier is presented as a precise control lever
edge_cases.failure_mode: overstated central-bank control of money stock
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether capital and loan-demand constraints are acknowledged
resolution: describe creation as demand- and constraint-limited

edge_cases.trigger: a liquidity run is explained purely as insolvency or vice versa
edge_cases.failure_mode: wrong remedy proposed for a crisis
edge_cases.example: recommending capital injection for a pure liquidity squeeze
edge_cases.detection_method: check that the diagnosis separates funding shortfall from capital shortfall
resolution: route remedy to the correct cause

edge_cases.trigger: a credit score is equated with a probability of default
edge_cases.example: treating a 720 score as a fixed default probability
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether the score is mapped to a calibrated PD before pricing
resolution: price on PD x LGD x EAD not the raw score

edge_cases.trigger: a feature proxies a protected attribute
edge_cases.example: a geographic feature standing in for ethnicity
edge_cases.detection_method: run a disparate-impact test against protected classes
resolution: remove or constrain the proxy feature

edge_cases.trigger: a payment is treated as final at authorization or clearing
edge_cases.example: releasing goods on an authorized but unsettled ACH
edge_cases.detection_method: check the stated finality point against the rail's actual settlement
resolution: identify the true finality point per rail

edge_cases.trigger: multilateral netting hides bilateral exposure until a member defaults
edge_cases.example: a defaulting participant unwinding a net batch
edge_cases.detection_method: check whether netting unwind and default scenarios are modeled
resolution: require collateral or loss-sharing in the scheme

edge_cases.trigger: a stablecoin peg is assumed robust without verified reserves
edge_cases.failure_mode: unanticipated peg break and redemption run
edge_cases.example: trusting an algorithmic peg under redemption stress
edge_cases.detection_method: check reserve verification and run-scenario analysis
resolution: apply run theory to the peg

edge_cases.trigger: a CBDC is designed without disintermediation safeguards
edge_cases.detection_method: check for holding caps, tiering, or remuneration limits

edge_cases.trigger: a payment or lending design omits AML/sanctions/fair-lending coverage
edge_cases.example: a cross-border rail with no sanctions screening
edge_cases.detection_method: check each activity against the compliance perimeter map

edge_cases.trigger: a clean explanation drops upstream uncertainty or caveats
edge_cases.failure_mode: a confident but wrong or unsafe conclusion
edge_cases.example: asserting a finality or solvency claim with no rail or caveat
edge_cases.detection_method: trace each claim to a node and source with stated caveats

workflow.objective: fix the money taxonomy and bank balance-sheet frame
acceptance_tests: money aggregates and bank-money distinction stated
workflow.do_first_because: the balance-sheet frame is the highest-coupling foundation every later mechanic inherits

workflow.objective: establish credit creation, funding/liquidity, and capital/solvency
acceptance_tests: capital distinguished from reserves and liquidity
workflow.do_first_because: core mechanics gate runs, monetary plumbing, and credit

workflow.objective: model the backstop, runs, and contagion
workflow.do_first_because: high-risk stability dynamics must be settled before synthesis

workflow.objective: model the credit lifecycle, expected loss, collateral, scoring, and spread
acceptance_tests: EL expressed as PD x LGD x EAD
workflow.do_first_because: credit risk and fairness must be settled before any lending claim

workflow.objective: establish payment layers and settlement finality
workflow.do_first_because: settlement theory gates rails, cards, and fraud

workflow.objective: compare rails and card networks and assess fraud/operational risk
acceptance_tests: fraud taxonomy mapped to rails and controls
workflow.do_first_because: instrument and fraud risk must precede payment recommendations

workflow.objective: model crypto ledgers, stablecoins, and CBDC tradeoffs
workflow.do_first_because: digital-money fragility must be settled before synthesis

workflow.objective: fix the regulatory, AML/KYC, and fair-lending perimeter
acceptance_tests: obligations mapped per jurisdiction and activity
workflow.do_first_because: the legal perimeter bounds every credit and payment recommendation

workflow.objective: integrate all mechanics into a grounded, caveated answer and validate
entry_criteria: stability, credit, payment, digital-money, and compliance outputs validated
acceptance_tests: every claim traced to a node and source
exit_criteria: human review complete for high-risk claims
workflow.do_first_because: synthesis must follow validated upstream mechanics to avoid laundering errors

workflow.objective: run iteration protocol, revalidate, and lock with change control
acceptance_tests: high-risk nodes human-reviewed before hard lock
workflow.do_first_because: locking before validation and review would freeze defects

priority_rationale.notes: credit creation gates plumbing and lending
funding fragility drives runs and margin
high-risk stability dynamics feed digital money and synthesis
expected loss underpins collateral, scoring, synthesis
architecture gates settlement and payment compliance
finality theory gates rails and cards
card rules gate fraud loss allocation
peg risk feeds CBDC and synthesis
perimeter bounds scoring and final answer

dominance_rules.trigger: a stakeholder wants a fast answer on a high-risk mechanic
dominance_rules.rule: high-risk claims (runs, solvency, peg, compliance) must be validated before release
dominance_rules.required_action: block release until the high-risk node is validated and reviewed
dominance_rules.example: refuse to call a bank 'safe' before run/solvency analysis

dominance_rules.trigger: a stressed bank requests liquidity support
dominance_rules.rule: diagnose solvency before applying liquidity support
dominance_rules.required_action: require a solvency check before recommending a backstop
dominance_rules.example: do not lend to a likely-insolvent bank as if it were illiquid

dominance_rules.rule: every loan must be priced above its expected loss
dominance_rules.required_action: reject growth that breaches the risk-appetite limit
dominance_rules.example: forgo market share rather than approve below price

dominance_rules.trigger: a feature improves accuracy but fails a disparate-impact test
dominance_rules.rule: fair-lending compliance dominates marginal predictive gain
dominance_rules.required_action: remove/constrain the suspect feature and document the tradeoff
dominance_rules.example: drop a proxy feature even at an AUC cost

dominance_rules.trigger: value release is requested before settlement finality
dominance_rules.rule: do not treat a payment as final before its true finality point
dominance_rules.required_action: gate value release on confirmed finality per rail
dominance_rules.example: hold goods until an ACH settles, not at authorization

dominance_rules.trigger: a new product would launch outside the compliance perimeter
dominance_rules.rule: no activity launches outside AML/sanctions/fair-lending coverage
dominance_rules.example: stop a new rail lacking sanctions screening

dominance_rules.trigger: a CBDC design risks bank disintermediation
dominance_rules.rule: cap CBDC features to protect deposit funding and stability
dominance_rules.required_action: apply holding caps or tiered remuneration
dominance_rules.example: limit a retail CBDC that would amplify runs

dominance_rules.trigger: a number is stated with unjustified precision/confidence
dominance_rules.rule: evidence-label correctness dominates apparent numeric precision
dominance_rules.required_action: label heuristic estimates as heuristic and avoid false certainty
dominance_rules.example: never present a heuristic PD as an observed rate

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision is reached
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates automation for irreversible/high-risk decisions
dominance_rules.required_action: escalate to a reviewer with a decision record
dominance_rules.example: require sign-off before a causation/compliance claim

dominance_rules.trigger: a fluent explanation lacks source/node grounding
dominance_rules.rule: every claim must trace to a node and source before it is issued
dominance_rules.required_action: attach node and source references with caveats
dominance_rules.example: reject a confident answer that cannot be traced

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the balance-sheet frame before any bank mechanic
anti_rework_rules.rationale: mechanics built on an undefined frame must be redone
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a mechanic refers to deposits as cash
anti_rework_rules.example: modeling credit creation before laying out the balance sheet

anti_rework_rules.rule: separate liquidity from solvency before diagnosing crises
anti_rework_rules.rationale: conflating them yields the wrong remedy and rework
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a crisis remedy ignores which shortfall exists
anti_rework_rules.example: prescribing capital for a pure liquidity squeeze

anti_rework_rules.rule: quantify expected loss before pricing or scoring a loan
anti_rework_rules.rationale: pricing before EL under-prices risk and forces re-pricing
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a rate is set before PD x LGD x EAD
anti_rework_rules.example: pricing a loan off a raw score

anti_rework_rules.rule: run fair-lending checks before deploying a scorecard
anti_rework_rules.rationale: deploying then discovering bias forces rebuild and remediation
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a model ships without a disparate-impact test
anti_rework_rules.example: launching a scorecard with a protected-class proxy

anti_rework_rules.rule: establish settlement theory before comparing rails or cards
anti_rework_rules.rationale: comparing rails without finality theory misranks them
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a rail comparison ignores finality timing
anti_rework_rules.example: ranking rails before defining settlement finality

anti_rework_rules.rule: characterize each rail's finality/reversibility before fraud analysis
anti_rework_rules.rationale: fraud loss incidence depends on rail finality
anti_rework_rules.example: analyzing wire fraud as if recoverable like ACH

anti_rework_rules.rationale: stablecoin risk is read off the ledger model
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: stablecoins described with no settlement model
anti_rework_rules.example: claiming stablecoin finality without the ledger

anti_rework_rules.rule: settle run theory before assessing stablecoin/CBDC fragility
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: a peg/CBDC risk claim ignores run theory

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the compliance perimeter before any credit/payment recommendation
anti_rework_rules.rationale: recommending outside the perimeter creates legal rework
anti_rework_rules.example: proposing a cross-border rail with no screening

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate upstream mechanics before integrating them
anti_rework_rules.rationale: synthesis over unvalidated inputs launders errors
anti_rework_rules.example: asserting a conclusion before run/credit analysis is checked

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or review reports a failure
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk and downstream impact
action: score defects by risk x coupling
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches high-coupling or high-risk nodes
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and priority_order
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the defect identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect is selected for repair
iteration_protocol.detection: route to the owning subsystem via repair_routing
action: recompute derived fields via the formula tool

iteration_protocol.trigger: evidence or inputs for a node change
action: flag nodes exceeding the revisit delta
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no node exceeds the posterior revisit delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: a high-risk or irreversible defect cannot be auto-repaired
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: high-risk defects resolved or formally accepted

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new KB version is produced
iteration_protocol.detection: compare against the prior version's checks and counts
action: diff checks and counts vs prior
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no regression or all regressions accepted

human_review_required_for: diagnosing a bank crisis as liquidity vs solvency
claiming a payment is final or a bank is safe
stablecoin peg or CBDC disintermediation claims
launching activity near the compliance perimeter
hard lock of the synthesis/decision protocol

checks.repair_action: split safety/return and CBDC/deposit tradeoffs into conflict edges
recomputed derived fields via formula tool

test_cases.input_summary: how does a bank create money when it lends
why did a solvent bank still fail
should this borrower be approved and at what rate
which rail to use for an irreversible high-value payment
is this stablecoin safe to hold
what are the risks of a retail CBDC

change_triggers: credit policy or risk appetite changes
payment rail or scheme rules change
version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked claim or compliance change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream mechanic changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
human_approval_required_for: claiming a bank is safe or a payment final
hard lock of the synthesis/decision protocol
